AI-Generated High (99 words): During a trip, a dark thought can show up that feels like the plain truth about you, like suddenly hating someone you love, or being sure you're a fraud. It's usually not the truth, just the opposite of whatever you were trying so hard to feel, coming into focus. Don't shove the thought down, because it'll just come back louder. Tell the person sitting with you if you want to, but don't go texting your whole family about it at 3 a.m., and don't decide you've got some lifelong disorder either.
AI-Generated Medium (11 words): Just notice the thought and the feeling that came with it.
AI-Generated High (36 words): They're intense, sure, but they aren't all of you. Then come back to the room you're in, your body, the person with you, what time it is, and, when you can, to love.

AI-Generated Low (69 words): Recognizing serotonin toxicity
We can use the Hunter criteria, the same checklist clinicians use to diagnose serotonin syndrome. One or more of these patterns makes the diagnosis more likely:
Spontaneous clonus: involuntary rhythmic muscle spasms, with no stimulation needed to set it off, would be one full pattern
Inducible clonus, spasms set off by stretching/flexing a muscle, plus agitation or sweating would be counted as one pattern altogether.
Human Medium (13 words): Ocular clonus (rapid involuntary eye movements) plus agitation or sweating, another pattern together.
